tone_statements.citation: Karan, Mark E. 1983. Comparaison entre les discours narratifs kabiyè et lukpa. In Jacques Nicole (ed.), Études linguistiques préliminaires dans quelques langues du Togo, 158-164. Lomé: SIL. (SIL id 18720)
tone_statements.quote: R. Pickering, à propos du lukpa, dit de l'aspect neutre: "This dependant form of the verb only occurs following other verbs which show aspect. It is always linked to the preceding verb by the connectives na or ilena, and is always preceded by the high tone form of the subject pronoun."
tone_statements.translation: R. Pickering says of the Lukpa neutral aspect: 'This dependent form of the verb only occurs following other verbs which show aspect. It is always linked to the preceding verb by the connectives na or ilena, and is always preceded by the high-tone form of the subject pronoun.'
tone_statements.locator: pp. 159-160 (sec. 2.2 'L'aspect des verbes'; fn. 3 = Pickering, Dompago Grammar, p.42; fn. 4 = Karan's French translation 'la forme à ton haut du pronom sujet')

tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.says: Discourse comparison, not a phonology; its only tone content is incidental but first-hand: quoting Pickering 1974:42, the Lukpa 'neutral' (aorist-like) dependent verb form 'is always preceded by the high tone form of the subject pronoun' (Karan's French gloss: 'la forme à ton haut du pronom sujet'), i.e. subject pronouns have tonally distinct (high vs non-high) forms with grammatical function. No tone inventory, TBU or sandhi statement. The host volume's other chapters are tone studies of Ditam…
